pages.hook: Many people in the USA treat their pets like family. Learn how to talk about a dog or a cat, and how to be polite when you meet someone’s pet.

facts.label: Before you pet a dog
facts.sub: Say “Can I pet him?” and wait for the owner to say yes.

facts.label: Pets have a gender word
facts.sub: People say he or she for a pet with a name, not it.

facts.label: A place for dogs
facts.sub: Many cities have parks where dogs can run and play.

facts.label: A short sleep
facts.sub: People use this phrase for a quick sleep, even for people.

pages.polite: Say **Can I pet him?** before you touch a dog. Say **He’s adorable!** to give a compliment.

mythfact.s: It is polite to ask the owner before you pet a dog.
mythfact.why: Some dogs are nervous. Always ask first.

mythfact.s: In English you say “It has three years” for a pet’s age.
mythfact.why: Say “He is three years old.” English uses be for age.

mythfact.s: “Cat nap” means a short sleep.
mythfact.why: It is a common phrase for a quick rest.

mythfact.s: “Curiosity killed the cat” means cats are dangerous.
mythfact.why: It warns people that too much curiosity can bring trouble.

mythfact.s: “Three Little Kittens” is a children’s poem about kittens that lose their mittens.
mythfact.why: Eliza Lee Follen wrote it, and it was published in 1843.

compare.br: In Brazil people say “Ele tem três anos”, and “vira-lata” is a popular word for a mixed-breed dog.
compare.us: In the USA you say “He is three years old.” People also say “mixed breed” or “mutt” for a mixed dog.
compare.tip: For age, always use am / is / are + number + years old.
compare.ask: Do you have a pet? Say its name and age in English.

quiz.why: Can I pet him? is polite.

quiz.q: How do you say the age of your cat?

quiz.why: A cat nap is a short sleep.

pages.title: Reading quest — My dog Max and a kitten called Luna · part 1
text: My name is Diego, and I live in **San Antonio**. I have a dog. His name is Max. He is three years old, and he is brown and white. “**So adorable**!” people say when they see him.

Last Saturday we went to the park. A woman said, “Look! What a cute dog!” “Thanks,” I said. “His name is Max.” She asked, “**How old is he?**” “He’s three years old,” I answered. “Does he like people?” she asked. “Yes, he loves people,” I said.

The woman has a cat called Luna. “**Aww**!” I said when I saw her photo. Luna is small and gray, and she sleeps all day. A **cat nap** is perfect for her! My grandmother says, “**Curiosity killed the cat**,” because Luna opens every box.

opts: A dog, a cat and two friends
fast.why: Diego talks about Max, Luna and the park.

scan.q: In which year did Eliza Lee Follen write the poem?

tf.s: Luna is a big black cat.

order: Diego goes to the park with Max.
A woman says Max is cute.
Diego says Max is three years old.
He sees a photo of Luna.
Max and Luna become friends.

opts: nice and sweet to look at

ctx.why: Sleeps = is in bed or resting.

ctx.sent: She opens every box because of her curiosity.

pages.think: Which pet would you like to have? Why?

pages.title: Reading quest — My dog Max and a kitten called Luna · part 2
text: In school, I learned a poem called “Three Little Kittens.” An American writer, Eliza Lee Follen, wrote it in 1843. Three kittens lose their mittens, and their mother is not happy. The kittens find the mittens in the end, and everybody is happy again.
Now Max and Luna are friends. They run in the park, and then they sleep. I love my little pet family.

text: My name is Diego, and I live in **San Antonio**. I have a dog. His name is Max. He is three years old, and he is brown and white. “**So adorable**!” people say when they see him.

Last Saturday we went to the park. A woman said, “Look! What a cute dog!” “Thanks,” I said. “His name is Max.” She asked, “**How old is he?**” “He’s three years old,” I answered. “Does he like people?” she asked. “Yes, he loves people,” I said.

The woman has a cat called Luna. “**Aww**!” I said when I saw her photo. Luna is small and gray, and she sleeps all day. A **cat nap** is perfect for her! My grandmother says, “**Curiosity killed the cat**,” because Luna opens every box.

In school, I learned a poem called “Three Little Kittens.” An American writer, Eliza Lee Follen, wrote it in 1843. Three kittens lose their mittens, and their mother is not happy. The kittens find the mittens in the end, and everybody is happy again.
Now Max and Luna are friends. They run in the park, and then they sleep. I love my little pet family.

opts: A dog, a cat and two friends
